links.outcome: AI tool technical adequacy across external sites, scanner models and manufacturers
links.effect: All three tools adequate in 97.7% of 11,699 exams from 777 institutions and 83 scanner models; 79 of 81 anisometry errors from one manufacturer, 80 of 81 on one scanner model.
links.quote: A total of 79 of 81 (97.5%) anisometry errors occurred on scanners from a single manufacturer; 80 of 81 (98.8%) occurred on the same scanner model.

links.outcome: Tool failure rate on external CT data differing from local development data
links.effect: At least one tool failed in 268 (2.3%) of examinations; individual adequacy 97.8% bone, 99.1% muscle, 98.9% fat.
links.quote: At least one tool failed in 268 (2.3%) of the examinations.

links.outcome: Failures from input specification mismatch (incorrect DICOM header voxel dimensions)
links.effect: Anisometry error accounted for 81 of 92 (88.0%) exams where all three tools failed; all three tools failed whenever it occurred.
links.quote: A single type of image processing error (anisometry error, due to incorrect DICOM header voxel dimension information) accounted for 81 of 92 (88.0%) examinations in which all three tools failed, and all three tools failed whenever this error occurred.

unlisted_practices: Using proper acquisition and reconstruction protocols to prevent preventable technical causes of AI tool failure

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the technical adequacy and failure modes (robustness across diverse external CT scanners) of automated AI body composition tools on multi-institution data, but does not test a specific deployment intervention or guardrail.
